record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Is every ℓ-group ℓ-isomorphic to Aut(Ω, ≤) for some partially ordered set (Ω, ≤) ?

evidence.quote: 1.35. (M. A. Bardwell [3]) Is every ℓ-group ℓ-isomorphic to Aut(Ω, ≤) for some partially ordered set (Ω, ≤) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group G equipped with a partial order ≤ such that (G, ≤) is a lattice and the group multiplication is order-preserving on both sides (i.e., a ≤ b implies xay ≤ xby for all x, y ∈ G). A homomorphism of ℓ-groups (an ℓ-homomorphism) is a group homomorphism that also preserves the lattice operations ∧ and ∨; an ℓ-isomorphism is a bijective ℓ-homomorphism.

For a partially ordered set (Ω, ≤), let Aut(Ω, ≤) denote the group of all order-automorphisms of (Ω, ≤), i.e., bijections f : Ω → Ω such that x ≤ y if and only if f(x) ≤ f(y). The set Aut(Ω, ≤) becomes an ℓ-group under composition together with the pointwise partial order f ≤ g ⇔ f(x) ≤ g(x) for every x ∈ Ω, provided this pointwise order makes Aut(Ω, ≤) a lattice.

Question: Is every ℓ-group ℓ-isomorphic to Aut(Ω, ≤) for some partially ordered set (Ω, ≤)?
